epithet: Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High
lede: The surah the Prophet ﷺ chose for the Friday prayer and for both ʿĪds. It opens with praise, promises him that he will not forget what he is taught, and names the choice that sorts people into two: this life, or the one that is better and lasts.

names.name: al-Aʿlā
names.note: After the name of Allah in its first ayah.

names.name: Sabbiḥ
names.note: Its first word, in full Sabbiḥi sma rabbika l-aʿlā. This is how the Companions referred to it, and Ibn Kathīr heads it Sūrat Sabbiḥ.

revelation.detail: Ibn al-Jawzī records agreement that it is Makkan; al-Qurṭubī gives it as the view of the majority and notes that al-Ḍaḥḥāk held it Madinan. Ibn Kathīr settles the matter with a hadith in al-Bukhārī: al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib, a boy of Madinah, says that the Prophet ﷺ had not yet arrived there when he had already learned “Sabbiḥi sma rabbika l-aʿlā” from the first emigrants. The traditional order places it eighth.

evidence.quote: سُورَةُ الأعْلى وَهِيَ مَكِّيَّةٌ كُلُّها بِإجْماعِهِمْ

وَهِيَ مَكِّيَّةٌ. وَالدَّلِيلُ عَلَى ذَلِكَ مَا رَوَاهُ الْبُخَارِيُّ: حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدَانُ: أَخْبَرَنِي أَبِي، عَنْ شُعْبَةَ، عَنْ أَبِي إِسْحَاقَ، عَنِ الْبَرَاءِ بْنِ عَازِبٍ قَالَ: أَوَّلُ مَنْ قَدِمَ عَلَيْنَا مِنْ أَصْحَابِ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ مُصْعَبُ بْنُ عُمَيْرٍ وَابْنُ أُمِّ مَكْتُومٍ، فَجَعَلَا يُقْرِئَانِنَا الْقُرْآنَ

attested.quote: أخْرَجَ ابْنُ الضُّرَيْسِ والنَّحّاسُ، وابْنُ مَرْدُويَهَ والبَيْهَقِيُّ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ قالَ: نَزَلَتْ سُورَةُ ﴿سَبِّحِ اسْمَ رَبِّكَ الأعْلى﴾ بِمَكَّةَ
attested.says: Ibn ʿAbbās: it came down in Makkah. Recorded by Ibn al-Ḍurays, al-Naḥḥās, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqī.
Makkan, in the saying of the majority.

setting: It is among the earliest surahs, from the time when the revelation was still new to the one receiving it. In those days, Ibn ʿAbbās relates of a similar passage, the Prophet ﷺ would move his tongue quickly as Jibrīl recited, afraid of losing a word. Here he is given the assurance in so many words: “We shall make you recite, and you will not forget — except what Allah wills.”

The rest of the surah is his commission in miniature. Remind — the reminder will benefit. Those who fear will take it to heart; the most wretched will keep clear of it. And success is defined, once and for all, in a single ayah: he has succeeded who purifies himself, remembers the name of his Lord, and prays.
It closes by saying that none of this is new. It is in the earliest scriptures, the scriptures of Ibrāhīm and Mūsā. The people of Makkah claimed descent from the first and had heard of the second.
aim: To remind souls of the favour of Allah, the Most High; to attach them to the life to come; and to free them from attachment to this lower one.

outline.title: Glorify
outline.summary: Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High: who created and proportioned, who measured and guided, who brought out the pasture and then turned it to dark stubble.

outline.title: The promise to the Prophet ﷺ
outline.summary: We shall make you recite, so you will not forget, except what Allah wills; He knows what is open and what is hidden. And We shall ease you towards ease.

outline.title: Remind
outline.summary: So remind, where the reminder benefits. The one who fears will take heed; the most wretched will avoid it — he who will enter the greatest Fire, and in it neither die nor live.

outline.title: Success, and what prevents it
outline.summary: He has succeeded who purifies himself, and remembers the name of his Lord, and prays. But you prefer the life of this world — while the Hereafter is better and more lasting.

outline.title: The oldest message
outline.summary: This is in the former scriptures: the scriptures of Ibrāhīm and Mūsā.

keyAyah.why: Three words in Arabic that the whole Qurʾan could be read as a commentary on.

virtues.text: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to recite, in the two ʿĪds and on Friday, “Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High” and “Has the news of the Overwhelming reached you?” And when an ʿĪd and a Friday fell on the same day, he would recite them in both prayers.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray the witr reciting “Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High”, “Say: O disbelievers” and “Say: He is Allah, One”.

When Muʿādh lengthened the night prayer for his people, the Prophet ﷺ said to him: “Why did you not pray with ‘Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High’, ‘By the sun and its brightness’ and ‘By the night when it covers’? Behind you pray the old, the weak and those with needs.”

before: Al-Ṭāriq told man to look at what he was created from. Al-Aʿlā begins with the Creator, and how He shaped and guided what He made.
after: Al-Aʿlā ends: the Hereafter is better and more lasting. Al-Ghāshiyah opens on it — the two kinds of faces there. The Prophet ﷺ recited the two together.
